title: LLM isolation: on Linux a cell cannot exec the CLI of its own family
summary: X4 masks LLM binaries on Linux with a bwrap bind of /dev/null. The mask also hides the binary from the launch of the cell, so bwrap masks only the other families, and a claude cell can still run claude -p (review of #1126, MEDIUM-4). Row N3 is darwin only. Accepted at shadow. Spec: docs/architecture/llm-isolation.md §7.1.
fix: Apply an exec rule after the exec of the CLI: a Landlock ruleset (LANDLOCK_ACCESS_FS_EXECUTE) or a seccomp filter that a small launcher sets and then execs the CLI, so the children of the CLI cannot exec the binary and the install roots. A bind of the CLI to a private path is rejected: the private path stays reachable.
acceptance: RED first: a Linux contract row (bwrap, stub CLI) that execs the own family from the cell fails before
The same row is denied after, and the launch of the cell still starts its CLI
Row N3 covers Linux; the darwin-only note leaves the matrix
Changed functions at 100% coverage on every CI OS; spec §7.1 updated
source: console, 2026-10-26, independent review of #1126 (MEDIUM-4); see docs/architecture/llm-isolation.md §7.1
